learned_hypothesis.statement: Inputs to torch.batch_norm_update_stats with zero elements and a zero size along the normalized dimension may exercise a numerical boundary in CPU execution where element count and normalized-dimension size are both zero, potentially exposing division-by-zero termination before input validation.
learned_hypothesis.abstraction_rationale: The Pattern's patch-derived mechanism indicates that this API computes a divisor from input size(1) and a numerator from total element count; for zero-element shapes where both are zero, the computation can evaluate to 0/0. Historical condition tc_01 provides one such zero-element shape and observed_failure confirms a floating-point termination, but the necessity of the exact shape and platform is not established, so the hypothesis generalizes only to a candidate zero-element/zero-dimension boundary and keeps the platform as a variation dimension.
limitations: The necessity of the zero-element shape is unknown rather than an established prerequisite, so this hypothesis does not assert that all such inputs will fail.
The platform condition is unknown and available evidence includes an observation of cross-platform difference, so platform dependence is not established.
The mechanism was inferred from the resolution patch and PR title rather than a mapped root-cause diagnosis.

variation_opportunities.statement: Vary zero-element input shapes beyond the reported case, including different zero/non-zero combinations along the normalized dimension, to explore which shape properties are involved in the numerical boundary.
Vary execution environment and device availability around the reported Linux CPU case to explore whether the boundary is platform-sensitive.

observation_candidates.statement: Observe whether zero-element inputs with a zero size along the normalized dimension result in a floating-point-style termination or a controlled error response.
Observe whether an empty-input invocation raises a controlled RuntimeError indicating a minimum-element requirement.
